note: Community-authored DP-700 practice questions from the MIT-licensed kengio/dp-700-study-guide repository, mirrored without their answer keys or explanations. The keys exist at the MIT source for reviewers; this site never presents them as validated. Hansa authored none of these questions.

questions.stem: A workspace admin enables high concurrency mode for notebooks so that multiple data analysts running similar ad hoc queries can share a single Spark session and reduce compute cost. No additional Spark properties are configured. Which statement about the resulting behavior is correct?

options.text: Up to 50 notebooks can share the session by default, and each is billed separately for its share of compute
Up to 5 notebooks can share the session by default, and only the initiating notebook is billed for the session
Up to 5 notebooks can share the session by default, and billing is split evenly across every attached notebook
Up to 50 notebooks can share the session by default, and only the initiating notebook is billed for the session

questions.stem: A tenant admin is troubleshooting a report that a user assigned to the "Sales" domain cannot open a workspace item, even though the user has Contributor access to the workspace. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Domain assignment doesn't grant or restrict item access — the issue is a workspace role or item-permission problem
The user's domain administrator must first approve their access before workspace roles take effect
Contributor role only grants access within the domain's default workspace, not others assigned to the same domain
The workspace must be marked as the domain's "default domain" before Contributor access is honored

questions.stem: A developer mounts a Lakehouse's `Files` folder via OneLake file explorer on their laptop. A colleague uploads a new file directly through the Fabric portal. Without the developer taking any action, what happens to that new file in the developer's local OneLake file explorer view?

options.text: It appears immediately, since OneLake file explorer keeps a full local copy in sync in both directions automatically
It appears only after the developer's laptop restarts, since sync runs on a boot-time schedule, not on file arrival
It never appears, since OneLake file explorer only reflects files the developer personally uploaded themselves
It doesn't appear until a manual Sync from OneLake, since remote changes aren't pulled automatically

questions.stem: A team wants to run Apache Airflow jobs in a Fabric workspace that is currently on a Premium Per User (PPU) license, and they also require the Airflow environment to run inside their organization's private VNet for compliance. Which statement correctly describes what's achievable today?

options.text: Both requirements are supported today, since Apache Airflow job runs on any licensed Fabric workspace with VNet support enabled
The VNet requirement is supported, but PPU workspaces must first be upgraded to a Fabric capacity before Airflow jobs will run
Neither requirement is achievable today — Apache Airflow job doesn't support Free/PPU workspaces or private networks/VNets
The PPU limitation is a licensing issue that support can waive; the VNet limitation is a hard platform constraint

questions.stem: A developer wants to both pull the latest changes from Git into their workspace and push their own uncommitted workspace changes to Git, in a single action. Is this possible in Fabric Git integration?

options.text: No — sync is always one-directional per action, Commit or Update, never both together
Yes, using the "Sync workspace" action, which performs Commit and Update together
Yes, but only for workspaces connected to GitHub, not for ones connected to Azure DevOps
No — Fabric requires disconnecting and reconnecting Git integration between a Commit and an Update

questions.stem: A team connects their Fabric Warehouse to Git for the first time and expects to need to hand-author a SQL database project to represent the schema before committing. What actually happens?

options.text: Git integration refuses to connect until a SQL database project is manually created and linked
The team must import the schema using SqlPackage before Git integration will recognize the Warehouse
A blank SQL database project is created, and every table must be defined manually before committing
Fabric automatically generates the SQL database project's schema — there's no manual authoring step

questions.stem: A team runs a deployment from the Test stage to the Production stage of a deployment pipeline. Production currently holds a Warehouse with 2 million rows of existing data, populated separately by a nightly load process. What happens to that Production data during the deployment?

options.text: It's overwritten with Test stage's data, since deployment pipelines synchronize both schema and data across stages
It's untouched — deployment pipelines never move data, only metadata and schema, regardless of direction
It's merged with Test stage's data using the Warehouse's primary key, avoiding duplicate rows
It's backed up automatically before the deployment, then overwritten with Test stage's data

questions.stem: A user with the Viewer role in a workspace wants to query a Lakehouse table using a Spark notebook via the OneLake APIs. Can they do this with just the Viewer role?

options.text: Yes — Viewer includes ReadAll by default, identical to every other workspace role
No — Viewer can't access the data at all, through any surface, including the SQL analytics endpoint
No — Viewer gets ReadData (SQL endpoint) but not ReadAll (OneLake APIs/Spark), which is Admin/Member/Contributor-only
Yes, but only if the Lakehouse owner explicitly grants the Viewer a separate Spark-execution permission

questions.stem: A Fabric Warehouse table has a row-level security policy applied via `CREATE SECURITY POLICY` with a filter predicate. A data engineer then queries the same underlying Delta table directly from a Spark notebook using the Lakehouse's OneLake APIs. What do they see?

options.text: The same filtered rows the RLS policy would return, since RLS is enforced at the storage layer
An error, since Spark can't read a table that has RLS applied through the SQL analytics endpoint
Only the rows the notebook's Spark session's SQL context allows, since Spark inherits SQL Server-style security policies
All rows, unfiltered — SQL-endpoint RLS applies only to SQL analytics endpoint/Warehouse queries, not Spark or OneLake API access

questions.stem: A security architect wants to apply a custom OneLake security role that restricts a specific user to a folder subset within a Fabric Warehouse's underlying OneLake storage. Is this achievable using OneLake security roles?

options.text: No — Warehouse isn't on the supported OneLake security role item-type list, unlike Lakehouse or Mirrored Database
Yes, as long as the Warehouse's workspace has OneLake security roles explicitly enabled at the workspace-wide settings level first
Yes, but only for read access — write restrictions via OneLake security roles aren't supported on Warehouse
No — OneLake security roles apply only to Spark-accessed items, and Warehouse is queried exclusively via T-SQL

questions.stem: A workspace Contributor queries a table with a dynamic data masking rule applied to a column. Do they see the real, unmasked values by default?

options.text: No — only the Fabric workspace Admin role can ever see unmasked values, regardless of any granted permission
Yes — Admin, Member, and Contributor workspace roles implicitly have the CONTROL permission that reveals unmasked values
No — UNMASK must always be granted individually per user, no matter their workspace role
Yes, but only if the column uses the default() masking function; other mask types always stay hidden from Contributor

questions.stem: A Power BI report, created independently in the Power BI service, has a "Confidential" sensitivity label applied. A data engineer then builds a Fabric Lakehouse-based semantic model that references data originally sourced from that report. Does the Lakehouse-side semantic model inherit the report's "Confidential" label?

options.text: Yes — sensitivity labels always propagate in both directions between Power BI and Fabric items
Yes, but only if the tenant has separately enabled mandatory sensitivity labeling
No — inheritance flows Fabric → Power BI, not the reverse; this is the one unsupported direction
No — sensitivity labels never cross between Power BI and Fabric items in either direction

questions.stem: A team needs to ingest data using a low-code connector-based extraction that a citizen developer maintains, then apply a custom fuzzy-matching algorithm that has no built-in equivalent, and finally trigger both steps on a schedule with a failure-notification branch. Which architecture best fits all three requirements?

options.text: A pipeline that schedules and sequences a Dataflow Gen2 activity followed by a Notebook activity, with an Upon Failure branch for notification
A single Dataflow Gen2 with a custom Power Query M function to replicate the fuzzy-matching logic, scheduled independently
A single notebook that both extracts the data with library-based connectors and implements the fuzzy-matching logic, scheduled independently
Two independently scheduled items — a Dataflow Gen2 for extraction and a notebook for matching — with no orchestration layer between them

questions.stem: A notebook is invoked three different ways over the course of a week: once by a user running it interactively, once as an activity inside a pipeline run, and once via its own independent schedule. For each run, whose identity does the notebook execute as?

options.text: The pipeline's own service identity in all three cases, since Fabric always executes notebooks under one shared identity
The workspace Admin's identity in all three cases, no matter how each of the three runs was actually triggered
The current user's identity in all three cases — execution identity never actually depends on the trigger type at all
It varies by trigger: current user, pipeline's last-modified user, schedule's owner

questions.stem: A notebook calls `notebookutils.notebook.exit("done")` inside a `try` block, wrapped so that a subsequent `except` block can catch and log the exit as if it were an error, when the notebook is invoked as a pipeline activity. What actually happens?

options.text: The pipeline activity completes normally with the exit value "done" — try/except has no effect on how `exit()` communicates with the pipeline
The `except` block catches and swallows the underlying `NotebookExit` exception, so the pipeline activity never receives the exit value
The notebook run fails outright, since `exit()` can't be called from within a try block in any context
The `except` block is skipped, but the pipeline activity is never marked as complete, leaving the run stuck

questions.stem: A nightly Spark job appends new order records to a Delta table using `df.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(...)`. After a transient failure mid-write, the job is automatically retried from the start using the same source data. The team then notices duplicate order rows. What's the most likely root cause?

options.text: Delta Lake's append mode is idempotent by default, so the bug must be in the source extraction, not the write
`append` is not idempotent — retrying it re-writes rows that already landed; a MERGE-based upsert is needed instead
The retry logic must have used `overwrite` mode instead of `append`, which caused the duplication
Delta Lake tables can't be retried safely at all; the pipeline needs a fully manual recovery process after any failure

questions.stem: A team implementing SCD Type 2 in a Fabric Warehouse using T-SQL wants to close out changed dimension rows and insert their new versions using a single `MERGE` statement, the same way their Delta-based Spark pipeline does it with the `mergeKey`-is-`NULL` trick. Is this achievable in T-SQL?

options.text: Yes — T-SQL `MERGE` supports the identical mergeKey-is-NULL pattern used in Delta MERGE INTO
Yes, but only if the table uses a Preview IDENTITY column as its dimension surrogate key
No — T-SQL SCD Type 2 needs two steps: a `MERGE` to close changed rows, then an `INSERT` for new versions
No — Fabric Warehouse T-SQL doesn't support `MERGE`, so SCD Type 2 needs `UPDATE` and `INSERT` statements only

questions.stem: A Spark Structured Streaming job writes directly to a Delta bronze table with no explicit output mode configured, and the team expects the write to automatically deduplicate and upsert records as they arrive. What should they expect instead?

options.text: The write defaults to append mode; upserts and dedup aren't automatic without an explicit `foreachBatch` + `MERGE` step
The write defaults to complete mode, fully rewriting the table on every micro-batch to keep it deduplicated
The write defaults to update mode, which automatically deduplicates on the table's primary key
The job fails to start, since Structured Streaming requires an explicit output mode to be set before any write can begin

questions.stem: A team of SQL Server-background developers needs to run `MERGE`-based load logic directly against curated star-schema tables, then have Power BI query those exact same tables afterward — no Spark, no separate BI-facing copy. One developer suggests a lakehouse, reasoning "it has a SQL analytics endpoint too, so the 'SQL' in the name means it can run `MERGE` just like a warehouse can." Is that reasoning correct, and which store actually fits?

options.text: Yes — every Fabric item's "SQL analytics endpoint" is the same read/write query engine, so lakehouse and warehouse are interchangeable for this load
No — Power BI can't connect to a Warehouse's SQL analytics endpoint at all in any tenant configuration, so only a lakehouse satisfies the reporting half
No — a lakehouse's endpoint stays read-only regardless of its name; only Warehouse's T-SQL surface supports the `MERGE` write
Yes, but only if the lakehouse tables are created directly under `/Tables` instead of via a shortcut, which unlocks full DML on the SQL analytics endpoint

questions.stem: A team creates a shortcut in a Lakehouse pointing to files in an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 container. They then configure caching on this shortcut to reduce repeated cross-region read latency. What happens?

options.text: Caching applies as configured, since ADLS Gen2 is one of the four cache-eligible external source types
Caching isn't available for this shortcut — ADLS Gen2 isn't on the cache-eligible source list
Caching applies, but only for files under 1 MB, since ADLS Gen2 has a stricter size ceiling than other sources
Caching applies automatically for all external shortcuts by default; no configuration step is needed or possible

questions.stem: A finance team mirrors their on-premises SQL Server database into Fabric using database mirroring. A business analyst asks whether they can write a correction directly into the mirrored table inside Fabric to fix a bad value, since it would be faster than waiting for a source-side fix. Is this possible?

options.text: Yes — mirrored tables support both reads and writes, since they're materialized as ordinary Delta tables
Yes, but only through the SQL analytics endpoint, and never through Spark or a notebook
No — mirrors stay read-only in Fabric; any correction must go back to the source system instead
No — mirrored data can't even be queried until the source connection is fully disconnected first

questions.stem: A team configures a Copy activity to land data into a Parquet file sink in a Lakehouse `Files` folder, and they want to enable the sink's "Upsert" write behavior so that matching rows are updated in place rather than duplicated. What do they find?

options.text: Upsert write behavior isn't available — it's a sink-side setting on database-family connectors only, not file-based sinks
Upsert write behavior works identically for file and database sinks, since Copy activity abstracts the difference away
Upsert write behavior is available for Parquet file sinks specifically, but not for CSV or JSON sinks
Upsert write behavior requires switching from Copy activity to Copy job, which supports it for all sink types including files

questions.stem: A developer calls `df.write.format("delta").partitionBy("region").saveAsTable("sales")`, expecting this to control how many in-memory partitions Spark uses while processing the DataFrame before the write. What does `partitionBy` actually control here?

options.text: Both the physical storage layout and the DataFrame's in-memory partition count simultaneously
Only the DataFrame's in-memory partition count during processing — it has no effect on how files are stored
Nothing measurable — `partitionBy` in `saveAsTable` is a no-op left over from earlier Spark versions
Only the physical storage layout (folder structure) — a storage optimization, not a partition-count control

questions.stem: A developer defines a `FOREIGN KEY` constraint between two tables in a Fabric Warehouse, expecting the engine to reject any `INSERT` that violates referential integrity, the same way it would in an on-premises SQL Server database. What actually happens on a violating insert?

options.text: The insert fails with a foreign-key-violation error, identical to on-premises SQL Server's default behavior
The insert succeeds — Warehouse constraints are `NOT ENFORCED`, informing the optimizer but never blocking bad data
The insert succeeds, but a warning is logged for the team to review and catch violations later on
The insert fails only when the constraint was created with an explicit `WITH CHECK` option specified

questions.stem: A team wants continuously aggregated, always-fresh rollup data in an Eventhouse table, updated automatically as new rows land, without any external orchestration. Which KQL mechanism is the correct fit?

options.text: An update policy referencing the source table with a fully qualified `database().table()` path
A `lookup` operator scheduled to run on a timer against the raw ingestion table
A standard `join` between the raw table and itself, scheduled via a pipeline every few minutes
A materialized view, which solves continuous aggregation with no external orchestration required

questions.stem: A T-SQL developer needs to replace NULLs across three columns of differing data types with fallback default values in a single expression, and wants the most standards-compliant, portable choice. Which function should they prefer over `ISNULL`?

options.text: `COALESCE` — it's ANSI-standard, accepts any number of arguments, with more predictable typing than `ISNULL`
`ISNULL`, since it's the Microsoft-native function and therefore always outperforms `COALESCE` in Fabric Warehouse
`TRY_CONVERT`, since it's the function designed specifically for cross-type NULL replacement
Neither — Fabric Warehouse requires a `CASE WHEN col IS NULL THEN ... END` expression for any NULL replacement

questions.stem: A team wants to apply a Filter operator directly before data lands in a KQL Queryset-backed dashboard destination inside their eventstream, the same way they can apply one directly before data lands in their Lakehouse destination. Is this configuration directly supported?

options.text: Yes — every eventstream destination supports a pre-ingestion operator identically, including a KQL Queryset
No — pre-ingestion operators are still Preview-only and not yet available for any destination at all
No — only Lakehouse, Eventhouse, Derived stream, and Activator support one directly; others need a derived stream first
Yes, but only if the KQL Queryset destination sits in the same workspace as the eventstream

questions.stem: A streaming aggregation query groups incoming events by customer ID and computes a running total, then writes to a downstream sink expecting only the rows whose totals actually changed in each micro-batch, not a full table rewrite. Which output mode fits?

options.text: `append`, since it's the default and works for any streaming query regardless of whether it aggregates
`update`, since it emits only the rows that changed since the last trigger, without rewriting the whole result table
`complete`, since it always contains the entire, latest result table on every single trigger
`complete`, since it's always required for any query involving a `groupBy` aggregation step

questions.stem: A team enables query acceleration on a OneLake shortcut pointing to Parquet files in ADLS Gen2, closing most of the performance gap versus a native Eventhouse table. They then try to attach a materialized view directly to that accelerated shortcut. What happens?

options.text: It fails — materialized views require a native table; even an accelerated shortcut remains an external table for this purpose
It succeeds, since query acceleration makes an accelerated shortcut behave identically to a native table in every respect
It succeeds, but the materialized view refreshes only once every 24 hours instead of continuously
It fails, but only because the source files are Parquet rather than a Delta-formatted source

questions.stem: A Spark Structured Streaming job uses a watermark to bound state for a windowed aggregation. An event arrives well after the watermark threshold has passed for its window. What happens to that late event?

options.text: It's rejected outright at the source and never enters the stream in any form
It's included in the next window instead, shifted forward to the nearest still-open window
It causes the entire streaming query to fail immediately with a late-data exception
It's silently excluded from its finalized window — a watermark bounds state retention, not entry

questions.stem: A pipeline's Notebook activity fails, and the pipeline's own run-history view shows only a generic activity-failure summary. The team wants the actual Spark-level error message and logs without leaving the pipeline monitoring experience to separately hunt through Monitor hub for the matching application. Is this possible, and how?

options.text: No — Spark execution detail is only reachable by searching Monitor hub separately for the matching application ID
Yes, but only if workspace monitoring is enabled and the pipeline is separately configured to log to the `ItemJobEventLogs` table first
Yes — inline monitoring deep-links the Notebook activity straight to its Spark execution details and logs
No — pipeline-triggered notebook activities don't produce a queryable Spark application at all, only ad hoc interactive runs do

questions.stem: A team needs to review Dataflow Gen2 refresh history older than what's shown in the 50-row UI list, going back several months. Where should they look?

options.text: Monitor hub, which retains Dataflow Gen2 history indefinitely beyond the 50-row UI limit
The refresh history persisted to OneLake, which retains up to 250 refreshes or 6 months, whichever is reached first
The detailed logs download, which covers the same 6-month window as the UI refresh history list
There's no way to see history beyond the 50 most recent rows; older refreshes are permanently discarded

questions.stem: A semantic model uses Direct Lake mode directly on OneLake (not via a SQL analytics endpoint). A query exceeds the Direct Lake guardrails for that model. What happens?

options.text: The query automatically falls back to DirectQuery against the model's SQL analytics endpoint instead
The query falls back to DirectQuery, but only when `DirectLakeBehavior` is explicitly set to `Automatic`
The query falls back to Import mode temporarily, until the model's next scheduled refresh runs
The query fails outright — OneLake mode has no DirectQuery fallback path

questions.stem: A team wants an Activator rule that fires specifically when a sensor's reported value crosses from below a threshold to above it — not just whenever the value happens to be above the threshold on any given check. Which condition type is required?

options.text: A stateful condition using `BECOMES`, since it tracks the value's change over time, not a single point
A stateless condition using a simple greater-than comparison, since Activator has no concept of value transitions
A stateful condition using `EXIT RANGE`, since crossing a single threshold is functionally identical to exiting a range
Either a stateful or stateless condition works identically here, since both evaluate the same underlying event stream

questions.stem: A team has two separate alerting needs: (1) fire when a batch of computed values from a scheduled KQL query exceeds a threshold, and (2) fire on values as they arrive continuously in a raw eventstream, before anything lands downstream. Which Activator alert source fits each need, and what's the default check frequency for the first?

options.text: KQL queryset alert (default 5-minute check) for the scheduled need; an alert set on the eventstream from the eventstream editor for the raw-arrival need
An alert set on the eventstream from the eventstream editor for both needs, since Eventstream can also run scheduled KQL queries directly
KQL queryset alert for both needs, since Eventstream doesn't support Activator as a destination
KQL queryset alert (default 1-minute check) for the scheduled-query need; Real-Time dashboard tile for the continuous raw-arrival need

questions.stem: A cloud-only Dataflow Gen2 refresh (no on-premises gateway involved anywhere in the chain) fails with "The dataflow refresh failed due to insufficient permissions for accessing staging artifacts." The team confirms the current dataflow's owner has full workspace Contributor access and signed in this morning. What's the most likely root cause, and where should the team look?

options.text: The dataflow owner's Contributor role needs to be manually upgraded to workspace Admin before staging artifacts become accessible again
The workspace's very first dataflow creator hasn't signed in for 90+ days, or has left the org
The workspace's staging capacity has been exhausted and needs a manual cleanup before the next scheduled refresh attempt
Dataflow Gen2 staging artifacts require the on-premises gateway's service account to be re-authenticated first

questions.stem: A Spark job in a notebook terminates with exit code 143 during a period when the team knows autoscaling was actively reducing node count. Should the team treat this as an out-of-memory failure requiring immediate remediation?

options.text: Yes — 143 always indicates OOM (SIGKILL) regardless of context, so remediation is always warranted
No — 143 always indicates a user code error unrelated to memory or scaling, so the team should review their code logic
Yes — any non-zero, non-one exit code indicates a genuine failure requiring the same OOM remediation steps
Not necessarily — 143 is SIGTERM, often a benign side effect of scale-down, distinct from 137 (OOM/SIGKILL)

questions.stem: An eventstream shows a healthy "Connected" status, and its Data insights panel confirms events are still arriving continuously from the source. Downstream, though, a Lakehouse destination is receiving data noticeably later than usual, and Runtime logs show no errors at any severity. What's the most likely explanation, and where should the team look first to confirm it?

options.text: The source's throughput-unit allocation, or the destination itself, can't sustain the rate — check Data insights' throughput panel
An `IncorrectDataFormat` error is being silently suppressed from Runtime logs — download the eventstream's own detailed logs to find it
The eventstream's connection has quietly dropped into an `EventHubException` state without updating its displayed "Connected" status
`AADSTS65002` is occurring intermittently, failing only a fraction of incoming events rather than the whole connection

questions.stem: A team tries to create a shortcut, using Delegated identity mode, to a source table that has RLS, CLS, or OLS security policies applied via OneLake security. What happens?

options.text: The shortcut is created successfully, and Delegated mode transparently enforces the source's RLS/CLS/OLS policies for every querying user
The shortcut creation is blocked — Delegated mode is intentionally prevented from targeting sources with RLS/CLS/OLS in OneLake security, by design
The shortcut is created, but RLS/CLS/OLS silently stops being enforced for any user querying through the shortcut
The shortcut is created only if the creating user personally has UNMASK/CONTROL permission on the source table

questions.stem: A team runs `OPTIMIZE` with both Z-Order and V-Order specified on the same table in a single command. In what order does Fabric apply these operations?

options.text: Z-Order runs first, then V-Order, then bin compaction last
V-Order runs first, then bin compaction, then Z-Order last
Bin compaction runs first, then Z-Order, then V-Order last
All three run simultaneously, in one pass with no defined order

questions.stem: A performance engineer wants to manually clear the Fabric Warehouse's in-memory/disk cache to get a clean baseline before a benchmark test, the same way they might clear a buffer pool on an on-premises SQL Server instance. Can they do this?

options.text: No — in-memory/disk caching is always on and can't be disabled; only result-set caching has a toggle
Yes, using `DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS`, exactly like on-premises SQL Server behavior
Yes, using `ALTER DATABASE ... SET RESULT_SET_CACHING OFF`, which clears both cache layers together
No — no caching of any kind exists in Fabric Warehouse; every query reads from storage fresh

questions.stem: A team enables Autotune on a notebook attached to a Runtime 1.3 environment with high concurrency mode also enabled, expecting Autotune to begin tuning `shuffle.partitions` after a handful of runs. What should they expect?

options.text: Autotune works as expected, tuning shuffle.partitions after roughly 20–25 iterations, unaffected by high concurrency mode
Autotune is incompatible with high concurrency mode — this combination won't tune as expected regardless of iteration count
Autotune tunes shuffle.partitions correctly, but only after 200 iterations instead of the usual 20–25
Autotune works, but only for `autoBroadcastJoinThreshold`, not `shuffle.partitions`, when high concurrency is enabled

questions.stem: A join between a large fact table and a dimension table is estimated at 15 MB at compile time — above the default 10 MB `autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` — so it starts running as a sort-merge join. Partway through, actual shuffle statistics show the dimension side is really only 3 MB after an upstream filter that stale statistics didn't account for. No `broadcast()` hint was written anywhere in the code. What should the team expect, and was a manual hint required to get a broadcast join here?

options.text: The join stays sort-merge for the entire run — only a manual `broadcast()` hint could have promoted it, since the compile-time estimate exceeded the threshold
AQE promotes the join to broadcast mid-query once real post-filter shuffle statistics confirm the dimension side is under the threshold — no manual hint was required
The join fails outright, since the compile-time size estimate exceeded `autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` and Spark never reconsiders that decision once execution starts
Raising `autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` to 20 MB before the run was the only way to get a broadcast join here, since AQE only tunes shuffle partition count, not join strategy

questions.stem: A team raises an Eventstream's throughput level setting to the maximum tier to fix slow processing, but the underlying Event Hubs source only has 2 partitions. What should they expect?

options.text: Throughput improves proportionally, since the throughput level setting is the only factor at play
Throughput improves, but only after the Event Hubs source is migrated to Kafka-compatible mode
No change, since Eventstream Processor CU never actually autoscales based on partition count
Little to no improvement — under-4-partition sources are bottlenecked regardless of throughput level

questions.stem: A lakehouse table backing a Direct Lake on OneLake semantic model runs a nightly `OPTIMIZE` job that compacts small files — the compaction changes which Parquet files exist, but doesn't add, remove, or modify a single logical row. Automatic updates are enabled on the semantic model. What should the team expect regarding reframing, and why does it matter even though no data actually changed?

options.text: No reframing is needed or triggered, since framing only reacts to logical row changes, and `OPTIMIZE` doesn't change any row's content
Reframing happens automatically, but only if `VORDER` was also specified in the same statement — a bare compaction doesn't register as a change at all
Automatic updates still reframes on the `OPTIMIZE` rewrite, since a later `VACUUM` could delete the pre-compaction files the model still references
`OPTIMIZE` is blocked entirely on any table feeding a Direct Lake on OneLake model, specifically to avoid this reframing question altogether

questions.stem: Finance needs a nightly, auditable pipeline that copies ERP invoice data from the on-premises SQL Server (via gateway), runs a Spark-based currency-normalization notebook, branches based on which regions actually submitted data that day, and emails the finance director if any step fails. Which orchestration approach satisfies all of these requirements?

options.text: Schedule the notebook independently, since notebooks can already read from a gateway-connected source and email on failure
Use a Dataflow Gen2 with a Power Query branching step, since Dataflow Gen2 natively supports conditional logic and email notifications
Use a pipeline with Copy and Notebook activities, an If Condition for per-region branching, and an Upon Failure notification path
Use Activator to detect a missing region's data and trigger the notebook directly, since Activator can run notebooks as an action

questions.stem: Fabrikam applies a T-SQL row-level security filter predicate on the Warehouse's shipment and invoice tables, keyed to each account manager's own region, and separately masks the `InvoiceAmount` column with dynamic data masking. Every account manager holds the workspace Contributor role, granted during the pilot so they could build their own ad hoc reports. When an account manager queries these tables directly, what do they see?

options.text: Every region's rows, with `InvoiceAmount` unmasked — Contributor bypasses both RLS and DDM entirely
Only their own region's rows, with `InvoiceAmount` still masked — Contributor bypasses neither control here
Only their own region's rows, unmasked — RLS still filters every role, but implicit CONTROL bypasses DDM
Every region's rows, but `InvoiceAmount` stays masked — Contributor bypasses RLS, not DDM

questions.stem: Dispatch supervisors need sub-second visibility into truck GPS location and engine-fault codes as they stream in, and the ops team that will build and maintain the dashboards is comfortable with KQL but not with writing Spark code. Which streaming architecture fits?

options.text: Route the eventstream to an Eventhouse (KQL database) for sub-second, code-free query latency
Route the eventstream to a Lakehouse table and have the ops team query it via the SQL analytics endpoint
Build a Spark Structured Streaming job that writes directly to a dashboard-ready table, since Spark offers the most control
Use Dataflow Gen2 to poll the telemetry source every few seconds and refresh a Lakehouse table

questions.stem: The 40 regional partners' daily CSV order-status extracts land nightly in an Azure Blob Storage container via SFTP. A transient failure occasionally causes the nightly job to retry, and the team has noticed duplicate order rows appear in the bronze Lakehouse table after a retry reprocesses the same day's file. What should they change?

options.text: Switch from a pipeline Copy activity to a OneLake shortcut pointing at the Blob container
Enable database mirroring on the Blob Storage account so retries are handled automatically
Reduce the retry count to zero, accepting occasional missed nightly loads instead of duplicate rows
Load into the bronze table using a business-key-based `MERGE`/upsert instead of a plain append

What does the pipeline's success status actually tell you about the dashboard's freshness, and where should the team look instead?

options.text: A successful pipeline run guarantees the Direct Lake model has also reframed — if the dashboard is stale, the pipeline status itself must be misreporting
Nothing — pipeline/notebook run success says nothing about whether a downstream Direct Lake model has reframed; check the semantic model's own refresh history Direct Lake tab separately
The pipeline's success status directly controls Direct Lake reframing as one of its own activities, so a green run always triggers a reframe automatically
Direct Lake models refresh continuously in the background regardless of framing events, so pipeline status is irrelevant and the dashboard should never show stale data

questions.stem: A cold-chain team monitors a vaccine fridge sensor that should stay within a 2–8°C band. They want an alert the moment the temperature departs that band on either side, and a *separate* alert if the sensor stops sending readings entirely for a stretch (e.g., a network outage). Which two stateful condition types fit each need respectively?

options.text: `BECOMES` fits both scenarios cleanly — it's Activator's general-purpose stateful operator for any kind of transition, range-based or missing-data driven
`EXIT RANGE` for the first; absence-of-data/heartbeat for the second — `BECOMES` doesn't fit either need as cleanly
A stateless comparison (`< 2 OR > 8`) is functionally identical to `EXIT RANGE` and simpler to configure, so use it for the first; heartbeat for the second
Neither requirement is achievable with an Activator condition — missing data and range departures both require an external monitoring tool outside Fabric

questions.stem: A semantic model's scheduled refresh has silently stopped triggering. No one manually disabled it. The team checks and finds the credentials for the underlying data source expired several days ago. What's the documented behavior that explains the schedule going silent, and what are the other two refresh-failure cause categories worth checking if credentials turn out fine?

options.text: Refresh schedules never auto-deactivate; the schedule must have been manually disabled by someone without leaving an audit trail

Credential failures alone can never cause a schedule to stop — only timeout and memory/capacity issues are documented as triggers for auto-deactivation, regardless of how many consecutive credential failures accumulate
A refresh schedule auto-deactivates after a single failure of any kind, immediately, with no consecutive-failure threshold
A refresh schedule auto-deactivates after 4 consecutive failures — credentials are one of three failure-cause categories, alongside timeout (default 5h/attempt, 24h total) and memory/capacity limits

questions.stem: Finance wants a data source rule configured for the MatchStats Warehouse's connection, expecting the same flexibility they already have for the leaderboard semantic model. What do they find when they try to configure it?

options.text: The data source rule configures successfully — Warehouse supports the same rule types as semantic model
Warehouse supports a data source rule but not a parameter rule, the same narrower support paginated report gets under deployment pipelines
No deployment rule of any kind is available for a Warehouse — connection differences for Warehouse need item-level parameterization instead
A data source rule is available for Warehouse, but only after first converting it to a mirrored database

questions.stem: The leaderboard's Direct Lake on OneLake semantic model refresh started failing outright with a guardrail error instead of just running slowly, after the backing Lakehouse table grew into the hundreds of gigabytes unoptimized. What's the fix, and could the team have expected a graceful DirectQuery fallback instead of an outright failure?

options.text: `OPTIMIZE`/`VACUUM` the source Lakehouse table; no — Direct Lake on OneLake never falls back to DirectQuery on a guardrail breach, it fails outright, unlike Direct Lake on SQL
Manually raise the model's guardrail thresholds in the semantic model settings; yes — a graceful DirectQuery fallback should have occurred automatically
`OPTIMIZE`/`VACUUM` the source Lakehouse table; yes — Direct Lake on OneLake always falls back to DirectQuery first, and only fails outright as a last resort
Nothing can be done once a guardrail is breached — the table must be rebuilt from scratch in a new Lakehouse

questions.stem: The trust & safety Contributor sees unmasked player emails during an investigation with no explicit `UNMASK` grant, while the Viewer on the same workspace stays masked. Both lack an explicit grant. What explains the difference?

options.text: DDM masking is randomly applied per session regardless of role, so this is expected variance, not a role-driven behavior
The Contributor must have an undocumented, hidden `UNMASK` grant applied automatically at workspace creation
Admin/Member/Contributor all carry implicit `CONTROL`, which bundles `UNMASK` — only Viewer, without that implicit privilege, stays masked
This is a misconfiguration — both roles should see the same masked view without an explicit `UNMASK` grant

questions.stem: A player's console reconnects and resends buffered match events several minutes after their 5-minute tumbling window closed. The streaming job's `.withWatermark()` tolerance has already elapsed for that window by the time the events arrive. What actually happens to those late events, and what's the precise role the watermark played?

options.text: The watermark automatically reopens the closed window and recomputes its aggregate to include the late events, since Delta tables support append-after-close by design and intent, the same way any append-only table recomputes a previously finalized aggregate
`.withWatermark()` has no effect on late data of any kind — its only documented purpose is exactly-once deduplication, entirely unrelated to windowed aggregation timing
The watermark rejected the events at the ingestion boundary — they never actually entered the stream and were silently dropped by Eventstream before ever reaching the Spark job

The events are still processed and land in the underlying data; they're just excluded from that specific tumbling window's already-finalized aggregation result, since the watermark had already bounded and released that window's state

questions.stem: A malformed anti-cheat detection payload arrives, and the `FlaggedSessions` update policy's transform query fails while processing it. The update policy is configured with `IsTransactional: true`. What happens to that batch's raw ingestion into the source table — does the trust & safety team still get the raw, unprocessed payload to investigate later?

options.text: The raw payload lands in the source table regardless, since transactional only ever affects the derived `FlaggedSessions` table's write, never the source ingestion itself no matter how the update-policy query is configured or how badly it fails
Nothing happens differently than non-transactional mode would — `IsTransactional` only changes logging verbosity, not commit behavior

The entire ingestion into the source table is rolled back — with `IsTransactional: true`, a failed update-policy query blocks the raw batch from committing at all, so there's no raw payload to fall back on for that batch
Only the malformed record within the batch is rolled back; the rest of the batch's raw payloads still commit to the source table normally
